searchText: also be aware of this: https://github.com/eth-clients Is there any reason to use the withdrawal queue for partial withdrawals? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2862 What exactly is the reason to still have a withdrawal queue for the partial withdrawals? I'd personally prefer if partial withdrawals could be accessible by everyone at any epoch instead of filling up the exit queue. it simplifies implementation to just have one withdrawal queue they are all withdrawals and the question is just how much of the validators balance can be stripped off based on their consensus lifecycle state and what that means for PoS security In what way do partial (up to leaving a balance of 32eth) withdrawals affect the security of ethereum? the security properties have more to do with where and how the validator's stake is at risk if i was a validator with say 20 ETH balance and i just suddenly withdrew 10 ETH, it would circumvent the gating mechanisms we use to ensure that any slashable behavior can actually materialize into a penalty against some real assset the way the protocol works today, any balance over 32 ETH doesn't really affect the protocol and is kind of just sitting locked at the CL so wrt security the protocol execution is isomorphic if we allow partial withdrawals of balance over this threshold withdrawals induce a load on the execution layer the queue bounds the load numbers can/should still be tuned to an appropriate load > instead of filling up the exit queue this is independent of the exit queue
